name: Cambridge Aerospace
summary: Cambridge Aerospace develops low-cost systems to counter drones and missiles. It raised a $300 million Series C at a $3.4 billion post-money valuation in August 2026, led by DFJ Growth.
overview: Cambridge Aerospace builds counter-drone and air-defence systems aimed at changing the cost equation of modern aerial warfare. Its product set includes drone interceptors, missile interceptors and radar systems for detecting and defeating threats.

facts.label: Latest financing
facts.note: The counter-drone company’s Series C was led by DFJ Growth.

bull_case: Cheap drones have made traditional interceptor economics increasingly difficult for militaries, creating demand for lower-cost alternatives. Cambridge's rapid funding growth gives it resources to turn product claims into deployments and larger defence programmes.
bear_case: Air-defence systems must prove reliability under demanding conditions and endure long procurement cycles. A $3.4 billion valuation after a short operating history leaves substantial execution and contract-conversion risk.
directory_notes: $300M Series C at $3.4B post-money in August 2026.

intelligence.description: A defence-technology company developing interceptors and sensors for counter-drone and air defence.
company: Cambridge Aerospace develops systems intended to detect and defeat drones and missiles, including Skyhammer drone interceptors, Starhammer missile interceptors and Looking Glass radar. The core strategic problem is reducing the cost mismatch between inexpensive attack drones and expensive legacy air-defence missiles.

The company raised a $300 million Series C at a $3.4 billion post-money valuation in August 2026, led by DFJ Growth. The round followed a reported $200 million Series B at a $1.3 billion valuation in April 2026, underscoring how rapidly investor interest in European counter-drone defence has grown.
intelligence.why_it_matters: Counter-drone defence is becoming a central procurement category as low-cost aerial systems reshape conflict. Cambridge Aerospace is an unusually highly valued private bet on whether a new generation of systems can deliver performance at economically sustainable cost.

changed.text: Raised $300M Series C at a $3.4B post-money valuation, led by DFJ Growth.

takeaways: The core thesis is lower-cost air defence against proliferating drones and missiles.
The $3.4B post-money valuation is tied to a reported August 2026 Series C.
System performance, production scale and defence-contract conversion are the crucial milestones.
